cards.f: How is the Periodic Table arranged?
cards.b: In order of increasing proton (atomic) number, in periods (rows) and groups (columns).

cards.f: Trend in character across a period
cards.b: Metallic on the left changing to non-metallic on the right.

cards.f: Why do elements in a group react similarly?
cards.b: They have the same number of outer-shell electrons.
Soft, low density (Li, Na, K float on water), low melting points; melting point decreases down the group.

cards.f: Group I trends down the group
cards.b: Melting point decreases, density increases, reactivity with water increases.
Forms hydroxide and hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Solution is alkaline.

cards.f: Why is potassium more reactive than lithium?
cards.b: Outer electron is further from the nucleus, less strongly held, so lost more easily.
Chlorine: pale yellow-green gas; bromine: red-brown liquid; iodine: grey-black solid.
Density increases, reactivity decreases, colour gets darker.
A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from its halide solution.
2KCl + Br₂ (solution turns orange); chlorine is more reactive than bromine.
High density, high melting point, form coloured compounds, often act as catalysts.
Unreactive, monatomic gases, because they have full outer shells of electrons.

cards.f: Predicting: reactivity of rubidium vs sodium
cards.b: Rubidium is lower in Group I so it is more reactive, softer, denser and has a lower melting point.

short.q: Describe what you would see when a small piece of potassium is added to water and write the equation. [4]
short.model: It floats, melts into a ball, moves quickly and burns with a lilac flame; 2K + 2H₂O → 2KOH + H₂.

short.q: Explain why the noble gases are unreactive. [2]
short.model: They have a full outer shell of electrons so do not need to lose, gain or share electrons.

short.q: Chlorine water is added to potassium iodide solution. State the colour change and write the ionic equation. [3]
Astatine is below iodine in Group VII. Predict its state, colour and reactivity. [3]
short.model: Solid, black/dark, and less reactive than iodine; it would not displace iodine.

short.q: State three properties of transition elements that are different from Group I metals. [3]
short.model: Higher density, higher melting point, harder; form coloured compounds and act as catalysts.
